statements.status_notes: CVE-2013-4441 reports that pwgen's phoneme mode, used unless -s is given, produces biased and easier-to-guess passwords. pwgen 2.08 still behaves this way, and upstream documents it: the pwgen(1) man page says passwords generated without -s should not be used where they could face an offline brute-force attack. The Debian security tracker lists 2.08-2 in trixie as unfixed, notes that memorable passwords are by design, and links Debian bug #726578, which is still open: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2013-4441. No upstream or distribution fix exists. Pending: a decision on whether upstream's documented position is a dispute that supports not_affected, or whether this stays open until a fix ships. Use pwgen -s for passwords that must resist brute force.
